summary: The Proposal defines resolveDefaultSchema() but never states that loadDefaultSchema() in bin/quay-native.ts actually invokes it, and no AC/DoD demands the CLI or MCP server fail closed (exit non-zero, no task created) on an invalid default_task_schema config value. AC5 only unit-tests the validator in isolation. This is the exact fail-closed wiring DIR-047 enforces (bin/quay-native.ts:100-101 'throws a clear error on illegal values — fail closed') and default-status.test.mjs section 3 tests ('with default_task_status set to an illegal value — CLI exits non-zero with clear error').
evidence: Proposal Changes #1-2 define resolveDefaultSchema and loadDefaultSchema but no invocation relationship; AC5 tests only the validator directly (assert.throws on resolveDefaultSchema); compare bin/quay-native.ts:100-101 and default-status.test.mjs section 3. AC8's 'mirrors default-status.test.mjs structure' clause is a process instruction, not a falsifiable production-callsite item. If the implementer forwards the raw value without calling resolveDefaultSchema, tasks are silently created with invalid schema values (fail-open).

summary: The mechanism claim (Proposal Changes #1: 'if frontmatter.extra.schema is unset and storeDefaultSchema is set, apply it to frontmatter.extra') applies equally when task_write passes extra with other fields but no schema, yet AC1 only falsifies the 'no explicit extra' case. The directive's motivating scenario is a creator passing extra: {acceptance: ...} and forgetting schema, so the untested sub-case is the primary use case.
evidence: Proposal Changes #1 vs AC1 ('no explicit extra'); 227 tasks in tasks/*.md carry 'schema: v1' in extra, corroborating the boilerplate-forgetting failure mode the directive targets.

summary: The Finding cites 'OUTER-LOOP.md line 28' for SELECT-time schema enforcement, but line 28 is the 'default concurrency=1 preserves backward-compat serial behavior' note; the actual schema_check(c) invocation is at OUTER-LOOP.md line 88 ('FAIL → fix task, block dispatch'). The substance (enforced at SELECT/block-dispatch) is accurate; only the citation is stale.
evidence: grep task-schema-check OUTER-LOOP.md → line 88; sed -n '24,32p' shows line 28 is the concurrency note. scripts/task-schema-check.sh exists and delegates to task-schema-check.ts.

summary: Review criterion 1 asks for explicit alternatives; the Proposal has no Alternatives section. It jumps to mirroring DIR-047 without documenting rejected options (e.g., applying the default at Core layer, hard-requiring extra.schema, validating in task-schema-check.sh at SELECT). A quality gap given the strong precedent, not a correctness issue.
evidence: Proposal structure: no Alternatives/decisions section; only Changes/Behavior/Non-goals.
